place.en: Armenia, Syria and the Phoenician coast
place.pt: Armenia, Syria and the Phoenician coast

stages.name: Other kingdoms
stages.desc: Pontus, Cappadocia, Iberia, Albania, Hasmonean Judaea and others

stages.name: Armenian
stages.desc: Ruled by Tigranes or paying him tribute

stages.name: Seleucid remnants
stages.desc: The last kings of the house of Seleucus

stages.name: Parthian
stages.desc: The Arsacid kings of Parthia and their vassals

stages.name: Roman
stages.desc: Roman provinces and lands held by Roman armies

stages.name: Free Phoenician cities
stages.desc: Tyre, Sidon, Byblos, Berytus and Arwad governing themselves

stages.name: Nabataean & Ituraean
stages.desc: Arab kingdoms of Petra and of the Lebanon mountains

states.name: Israel
timeline: Hasmonean Judaea under Alexander Jannaeus; Ptolemais stands apart on the coast
Salome Alexandra succeeds her husband Jannaeus as queen
Tigranes takes Ptolemais; Salome Alexandra buys him off with gifts
Tigranes's army withdraws north to face Lucullus
Salome Alexandra dies; her sons Hyrcanus and Aristobulus fight for the throne

states.name: Lebanon
timeline: Tyre, Sidon, Berytus and Byblos govern themselves; Ituraeans hold the mountains
The coast passes under the overlordship of Tigranes
Tigranes withdraws; the cities fend for themselves against Ituraean raids
Pompey confirms the freedom of Tyre and Sidon inside his new province

states.name: Syria
timeline: Seleucid princes fight one another for Antioch and Damascus
The Syrians hand their crown to Tigranes; Magadates governs from Antioch
Tigranes's troops withdraw; Lucullus recognises Antiochus XIII at Antioch
Pompey deposes the last Seleucid king and makes Syria a Roman province

states.name: Georgia
timeline: The kingdom of Iberia in the Caucasus
Pompey defeats King Artoces of Iberia and takes hostages

states.name: Azerbaijan
timeline: Caucasian Albania along the Kura river
Armenia's eastern provinces reach the Kura; Tigranes's power dominates
Pompey defeats the Albanian king Oroezes on the Kura

states.name: Turkey
timeline: Pontus, Cappadocia, Bithynia and smaller kingdoms; Rome holds the province of Asia in the west
Tigranes invades Cappadocia on behalf of Mithridates of Pontus
Tigranes builds Tigranocerta and rules the south-east, Commagene and Cilicia
Lucullus takes Tigranocerta; Roman armies dominate Anatolia
Pompey defeats Mithridates; Pontus is joined to Rome's provinces

states.name: Armenia
timeline: Tigranes II takes the throne at Artaxata after years as a hostage in Parthia
Sophene is annexed: the two Armenian kingdoms are united
Lucullus wins by the Arsanias, but his army turns back before Artaxata
Tigranes submits to Pompey at Artaxata and keeps Armenia as Rome's ally

states.name: Iraq
timeline: Parthian Mesopotamia, from Nisibis to Seleucia on the Tigris
Tigranes takes Adiabene, Gordyene and Nisibis from a weakened Parthia
Lucullus storms Nisibis, the Armenian stronghold of the north
Phraates III of Parthia, now Pompey's ally, moves back into the north

states.name: Iran
timeline: Parthian Iran under Mithridates II
Media Atropatene, in the north-west, becomes Tigranes's vassal
Phraates III allies with Pompey and invades Armenia

states.name: Jordan
timeline: The Nabataean kingdom of Petra controls the incense roads
Aretas III defeats Antiochus XII and takes Damascus
Nabataea stays independent as Pompey reaches Syria

events.title: Tigranes crowned
events.text: Freed from Parthian captivity for seventy valleys of land, Tigranes takes the Armenian throne.

events.title: Seleucus VI
events.text: Seleucus VI defeats his uncle Antiochus IX and takes Antioch, but holds it barely a year.

events.title: Sophene annexed
events.text: Tigranes deposes the king of Sophene and unites the Armenian lands.

events.title: Death at Mopsuestia
events.text: Driven out of Syria, Seleucus VI is burned alive by a mob in Cilicia.

events.title: Pontic marriage
events.text: Tigranes marries Cleopatra, daughter of Mithridates VI of Pontus.

events.title: Cappadocia invaded
events.text: For his father-in-law, Tigranes drives the Roman-backed king Ariobarzanes out of Cappadocia.

events.title: Sulla on the Euphrates
events.text: The Roman Sulla receives a Parthian embassy on the Euphrates: Rome's first contact with Parthia.

events.title: Asian Vespers
events.text: Mithridates orders the massacre of Romans and Italians in Asia, starting his first war with Rome.

events.title: Parthia falters
events.text: The death of Mithridates II leaves Parthia divided between rival kings.

events.title: Demetrius III captured
events.text: Besieging his brother Philip at Beroea, Demetrius III is taken by Parthian allies and dies in captivity.

events.title: King of Kings
events.text: Tigranes recovers the seventy valleys, takes Adiabene and Gordyene and adopts the Persian title King of Kings.

events.title: Atropatene submits
events.text: The kings of Media Atropatene become Tigranes's vassals.

events.title: Aretas takes Damascus
events.text: Antiochus XII dies fighting the Nabataeans; their king Aretas III takes Damascus.

events.title: Tigranes in Antioch
events.text: Weary of civil war, the Syrians offer their crown to Tigranes; Magadates governs for him.

events.title: Selene at Ptolemais
events.text: Cleopatra Selene, widow of three Seleucid kings, holds Ptolemais for her son Antiochus.

events.title: Tigranocerta
events.text: Tigranes founds a new royal city named after himself on the upper Tigris.

events.title: Arwad's harbour
events.text: The island city of Arwad keeps its own council, fleet and coinage.

events.title: Cappadocia emptied
events.text: Tigranes deports the people of Mazaca and other Greek cities to fill Tigranocerta.

events.title: Salome Alexandra
events.text: Alexander Jannaeus dies; his widow Salome Alexandra rules Judaea.

events.title: Selene's sons
events.text: Selene sends her sons to Rome to claim Egypt's throne; the Senate sends them home empty-handed.

events.title: Bithynia to Rome
events.text: King Nicomedes IV leaves Bithynia to Rome; Mithridates opens his third war.

events.title: Cyzicus relieved
events.text: Lucullus traps Mithridates's army besieging Cyzicus and starves it out.

events.title: Cabira
events.text: Defeated by Lucullus at Cabira, Mithridates flees to his son-in-law in Armenia.

events.title: Damascus Armenian
events.text: Tigranes's forces take Damascus from the Nabataeans.

events.title: Appius at Antioch
events.text: Lucullus's envoy Appius Claudius demands the surrender of Mithridates; Tigranes refuses.

events.title: Sinope falls
events.text: Lucullus takes Amisus and Sinope; Pontus is in Roman hands.

events.title: Siege of Ptolemais
events.text: Tigranes besieges and takes Ptolemais; Selene is captured.

events.title: Gifts from Jerusalem
events.text: Queen Salome Alexandra sends envoys and gifts to keep Tigranes out of Judaea.

events.title: Lucullus crosses
events.text: Lucullus crosses the Euphrates into Tigranes's lands.

events.title: Battle of Tigranocerta
events.text: On 6 October, Lucullus routs Tigranes's army; the city is opened and plundered.

events.title: Selene put to death
events.text: Tigranes has Cleopatra Selene executed at Seleucia, a fortress on the Euphrates.

events.title: Antiochus XIII
events.text: Lucullus recognises Selene's son Antiochus XIII as king in Antioch.

events.title: The Arsanias
events.text: Lucullus beats Tigranes again by the Arsanias, but his army refuses to march on Artaxata.

events.title: Nisibis stormed
events.text: In winter, Lucullus's army takes Nisibis and Tigranes's treasure.

events.title: Zela
events.text: Mithridates destroys a Roman army at Zela as Lucullus's legions mutiny.

events.title: Pirates cleared
events.text: Pompey sweeps the pirates from the sea and takes their last fortresses in Cilicia.

events.title: Night battle
events.text: Pompey surprises and crushes Mithridates's army by night near the Lycus.

events.title: Tigranes submits
events.text: Tigranes lays his diadem at Pompey's feet near Artaxata; Pompey hands it back.

events.title: Albania and Iberia
events.text: Pompey fights the Albanians on the Kura and the Iberians in the Caucasus.

events.title: Damascus occupied
events.text: Pompey's legates occupy Damascus.

events.title: Syria annexed
events.text: At Antioch, Pompey refuses the Seleucids their kingdom; Syria becomes a Roman province.

events.title: Tyre and Sidon free
events.text: Pompey confirms Tyre and Sidon as free cities with their own laws and coins.

events.title: Tyrants beheaded
events.text: Pompey executes the tyrant of Tripolis; Byblos is freed from the tyrant Cinyras.

events.title: Ituraean ransom
events.text: Ptolemy son of Mennaeus, Ituraean lord of Chalcis, pays a thousand talents to keep his lands.

chartNote: Share of the area of ten present-day countries (today's boundaries; Iran is cut at the map's edge), by the power that dominated most of each, or the part this story is about. Ancient rule was a web of vassals and tribute rather than borders, so this is a strong simplification: Turkey, for example, also held Pontus and Roman Asia when the map shows it Armenian.
